references_named: Robert Rauschenberg, This Is a Portrait of Iris Clert If I Say So (1961)
rationale: The URL hash binding is a textbook P1 move: the address bar literally is the notary of the portrait, so the mechanism enacts Rauschenberg's authorship-by-assertion rather than illustrating it. The build is the smallest possible (one sentence, one frame, one hash) and the wall label — 'Medium: the address bar,' 'Authenticity: my word' — lands the double-coding cleanly without requiring wall text. It answers a specific prior work (Rauschenberg's 1961 telegram) and sits firmly on the order end of the chance/order axis, extending the catalogue's argument that web plumbing already embodies canonical conceptual gestures.
reservations: The Rauschenberg reference is well-trodden in conceptual art discourse, so the novelty of the found-object is moderate rather than high; the freshness lives almost entirely in the web-native re-staging. The dialogue with the broader y-a-v-a catalogue (e.g., how this sits next to 'But is it art?' or 'The Original') is implicit rather than explicit.
revision_suggestion: Consider a small secondary layer that makes the connection to the broader twenty-year argument more legible — e.g., a footer line naming one prior y-a-v-a work this answers, or a subtle visual echo of an existing piece — to strengthen the narrative thread without adding weight.
